content:
Molly S: filing an escalation for AcmeCorp — they're seeing 250-400ms extra p99 latency and intermittent 401s for EU customers since 06:45 UTC. They claim requests are landing in us-east-1 despite using eu-west-1 endpoints and region headers.

Dheeraj K: do we have a customer request id or sample request?

Molly S: request-id=acme-req-20260317-1122, sample curl below. They set X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 but response headers show X-Forwarded-Region: us-east-1 and X-Envoy-Cluster: model-us-east-1.

Molly S: ```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-neox-20b","input":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< X-Forwarded-Region: us-east-1
< X-Envoy-Cluster: model-us-east-1
< X-Request-Id: acme-req-20260317-1122
```

Ingrid L: thanks — initial thought: L7 gateway header rewrite + fallback routing. We've seen a bug where on backend fallback (when preferred region capacity is busy) the region hint header gets replaced with default region by the proxy, causing sticky sessions to cross-region.

Alex P: checking LB/Envoy config now. Can someone paste tracing for that request id? ops-bot should have the trace if tracing header present.

Ops-bot: trace found for acme-req-20260317-1122: 
- ingress-gateway -> route-match -> matched cluster: model-eu-west-1 (initial) -> cluster health unstable -> fallback to model-us-east-1 (policy: regional-fallback) -> header_rewrite filter applied -> set X-Forwarded-Region=us-east-1 -> downstream response returned.

Dheeraj K: that sequence matches their experience. But why 401s? If token audience is region-bound we could see 401 when token issued for eu-west but validated against us-east public key set. Any auth logs?

Ingrid L: auth logs show JWT validated against jwks-us-east for ~30% of requests that were routed to us-east; other times they succeed. Looks like intermittent fallback plus header rewrite causes auth to pick the wrong jwks cache (we key off X-Forwarded-Region in auth middleware).

Maria R: Customer also flagged a billing spike concurrently: more retries and longer token refresh loops. We should include billing team in the loop.

Alex P: reproduced locally with a canary of the region-fallback policy. Repro steps:
1) Deploy a pretend capacity-saturated response from cluster eu-west.
2) Send 50 concurrent requests with header X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1.
3) Observe route decision then header_rewrite setting X-Forwarded-Region to default on fallback.

Alex P: ```yaml
# minimal envoy snippet showing problematic filter order
- name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
  typed_config:
    "http_filters":
    - name: envoy.filters.http.router
    - name: envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata
      # this one runs after router on fallback in our canary
```

Ingrid L: aha — filter order reversed in the fallback path for the canary build we rolled last week. header_rewrite runs after the routing decision in that code path which causes auth to see the rewritten region instead of the request hint.

Dheeraj K: is this limited to the canary? Which ASGs/hosts are on the bad build?

Ops-bot: bad-build tag: gateway-v2.3.7-canary is running on hosts: gw-eu-*-canary (10.11.20.0/24) and a small slice in prod-eu.

Molly S: customer is on EU prod region, calls are hitting the canary hosts due to load steering. They're extremely sensitive — can we isolate?

Alex P: we can remove canary from the EU LB pool (start drain) — will take ~2 minutes for active drains to finish. Propose immediate rollback of gateway-v2.3.7-canary in eu.

Ingrid L: also need to mitigate auth selection: make auth fallback tolerant to both JWKS sets while we fix header ordering (short-term hotfix: if X-Redwood-Region present prefer it over X-Forwarded-Region for jwks lookup).

Dheeraj K: agree. I'll push a config change to auth middleware to prefer client-supplied X-Redwood-Region if present and mapping to a known region, with a 5m helm rollout.

Maria R: I'll notify billing ops and AcmeCorp's CSM that we're rolling a canary drain + auth config hotfix. Please include expected ETA and whether they should throttle.

Molly S: they've already started rate-limiting on their side but asked for we to pause/cancel any retries. CSM wants rollback confirmation.

Ops-bot: rollback initiated for gateway-v2.3.7-canary in eu cluster. Start drain 1974501245.

Alex P: draining hosts now, removing from LB weight. Will monitor p99 and auth 401 rate.

Ingrid L: deploying auth middleware change to prefer X-Redwood-Region (short-term) — will patch config across eu gateways now.

Dheeraj K: config change applied at 1974501268. Monitoring logs: auth jwks selection shifted to jwks-eu for requests with X-Redwood-Region. 401 rate dropping in canary logs.

Ops-bot: drain complete, canary instances out of rotation at 1974501279.

Alex P: metrics: p99 latency for Acme dropped from 420ms->160ms in last 2m. 401 rate dropped 82% -> 8%.

Molly S: sharing this with AcmeCorp: rollback + hotfix applied, monitoring. They asked for RCA and timeline for a permanent fix.

Ingrid L: next steps for RCA:
- root cause: header_rewrite filter ordering introduced in gateway-v2.3.7-canary caused fallback path to rewrite region header after route selection, causing auth to use wrong jwks.
- short-term mitigation: rollback canary + auth middleware preference for X-Redwood-Region.
- permanent fix: adjust filter ordering and add integration test that asserts region header preservation across fallback and route rewrite cases; patch and release gateway-v2.3.8.

Dheeraj K: tagging eng-runtime oncall and release engineering for the permanent patch. I'll open follow-up ticket and link this thread.

Maria R: noted — billing ops engaged, CSM loop closed for now. Will keep customer informed.

Molly S: thanks everyone. I'll close once customer ack and billing check confirmed. :thumbsup:
